title: Secret of the Tohto Film Development Studio
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ai Haibara, the Detective Boys, Professor Agasa, Yukiko Kudo) omitted by convention, same as ep011. The old cases/ file's culprit (s3 Negami) is CORRECT per the transcript, but its single 'Fluorescent tape and paint' object conflates two separate facts and gets them backwards on ownership: the tape marking corners around Hojima's apartment (concealed under black tape) was placed by the VICTIM, Furumura, for his own nighttime trips to the toilet -- not by Negami, and not for navigating a crime. The only thing Negami actually did was secretly coat the victim's third shirt button in the same kind of fluorescent paint three days earlier (while Furumura was passed out from all-night mahjong), so he could locate his heart precisely once the room went dark; he then exploited Furumura's own pre-existing tape trail to move silently, rather than having set up the room himself. This distinction (whose tape is whose) is the actual twist Conan explains, and matters structurally since it separates victim-authored evidence from culprit-authored evidence. Old file also omits: the darkroom/rest-area alibi locations, the spare-key access shared by three people, the torn-and-later-returned button that was the actual trap Conan used to catch Negami, and the fact that all three male suspects (Hojima, Karata, Negami) were floated as having a professional grudge against Furumura before narrowing to Negami. No event nodes: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Silence contradiction: escaping such a cluttered, pitch-dark room fast enough should have caused noise, but neither the sleeping children next door nor the victim's own running video camera recorded any -- proves the culprit could navigate the dark room confidently, pointing to darkroom-trained staff rather than random chance.

Timing comparison: Furumura hadn't changed his dirty shirt in days (confirmed by mahjong three days earlier), so fluorescent paint applied to his button that day would still be marking his heart's position on the night of the murder -- only someone who knew both his hygiene habits and darkroom marking technique could have planned this.
